discovery: Conformal field theory of two-dimensional critical phenomena (infinite conformal symmetry and exact solution of critical systems)

nominees.name: Alexander A. Belavin
nominees.affiliation: Landau Institute for Theoretical Physics, Russia

subfield: Statistical physics and quantum field theory
motivation: In 1984 Belavin, Polyakov and Zamolodchikov showed that at a two-dimensional critical point scale invariance extends to an infinite-dimensional conformal symmetry. From this single principle they derived exactly the critical exponents and correlation functions of whole classes of systems (Ising, Potts, tricritical and percolation-like models), turning the renormalization-group picture into an exactly solvable theory. Polyakov had earlier recognised conformal invariance of critical fluctuations; Zamolodchikov added the c-theorem and integrable perturbations away from criticality. The framework predicted measured exponents in thin films, adsorbed monolayers and quantum Hall edges, underlies the theory of one-dimensional quantum systems and quantum computing benchmarks, and inspired Schramm-Loewner evolution and the modern conformal bootstrap, which now gives the most precise 3D Ising exponents. It is a rare case of a simple symmetry idea revealing hidden order in complex fluctuating matter, with consequences across condensed matter, string theory and mathematics.
